terms.grammar: deponent verb, fourth conjugation, with the dative
evidence: Plin. NH 34.19.88: mātrī … īnfante miserābiliter blandiente (Lewis & Short: “to fawn upon, to flatter, soothe, caress, coax”)

terms.latin: palpor, palpārī, palpātus sum (palpō, palpāre) (+ dat.)
terms.gloss: stroke, pat; and so coax, wheedle, soft-soap
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 507: observātōte eum, quam blandē mulierī palpābitur
Hor. S. 2.1.20: cui male sī palpēre, recalcitrat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly of stroking an animal with the hand (equum palpārī).

phrases.latin: observātōte eum, quam blandē mulierī palpābitur
phrases.english: just watch how sweetly he’ll coax the lady

sources: Lewis & Short: blandior · Lewis & Short: palpo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 316.
